text:
sara-ml: quick heads-up — I finished the KV-only mixed-precision bakeoff for the new llama-variant. summary: FP8 on KV matrices + INT8 elsewhere yields the best memory/latency combo but has small generative deltas on long-context prompts.

sara-ml: put the raw numbers in gs://redwood-inference/kv-bakeoffs/mixed-kv-1912345678/results.csv and a short notebook with evals.

mike-ops: nice. what's the baseline here (fp16 across the board)?

sara-ml: baseline is fp16 everywhere. compared to that: memory -40% median, p95 token-latency -8% in steady state for long sequences (8k), throughput +12% for batch-4.

eva-research: what about quality? any catastrophic regressions on our eval sets?

sara-ml: most evals are within noise. we saw a consistent ~0.6% drop on the long-context summarization rubric and occasional hallucination spikes on a tiny fraction of prompts (0.2% of test set).

sara-ml: attaching the delta table (columns: eval_set, metric, baseline, mixed-kv, delta) and a quick diff of tokens where the model diverged.

raj-mleng: can you paste the bench command? want to reproduce on a local dedicated node.

sara-ml: sure — this is the runner I used:

```
# run on a single A100-80GB dedicated node
python bench_kv.py \
  --model redwood/llama-var:v2 \
  --kv-quant-profile kv_fp8_int8_mix.json \
  --context 8192 \
  --batch 4 \
  --warmup 200 \
  --measure tail,p95,mem
```

raj-mleng: thanks. what's inside kv_fp8_int8_mix.json roughly?

sara-ml: per-layer mapping, e.g. KV projection layers = fp8-e4m3, attention q/k/v = fp8, output + ffn matmuls = int8 symmetric. also use per-channel scales and a small dequant bias fix we experimented with.

ci-bot: perf-check results uploaded: gs://ci-artifacts/1912345678/perf.json :white_check_mark:

mike-ops: any stability issues in the runtime with fp8 kernels? crashes?

sara-ml: no crashes in ~300 runs, but observed occasional tiny numerical underflows during very short sequences which we patched with an epsilon in the quant pipeline. logged as PR #842 in infra.

eva-research: for the 0.6% summary drop, can we run selective higher-precision fallback on the attention output for steps > 4k? might recover quality while keeping mem benefits.

sara-ml: that's our hypothesis. i ran a quick canary: enabling fp16 fallback only for the final linear after attention on long windows recovers ~0.45% of that drop and costs ~6% extra memory — net still wins.

raj-mleng: what about KV cache size math? numbers?

sara-ml: example: 8k tokens @ hidden=4096: baseline KV mem ~ 6.4GB, mixed-kv ~ 3.9GB. after enabling final-linear fp16 fallback it goes to ~4.2GB.

mike-ops: good. any perf regression on cold-start / first token?

sara-ml: slightly slower 1st-token compute (~+4ms) because of extra cast path, but steady-state p50/p95 improved.

eva-research: next steps from my side: run the mixed profile on the control eval set with longer prompt perturbations, and try AWQ quant for comparison on the same KV-only scheme.

sara-ml: yes, planning to add AWQ and GPTQ runs into the same spreadsheet. ETA EOD tomorrow for updated numbers.

raj-mleng: i'll spin a dedicated node with the profile and try an A/B on the canary route in staging (cc @mike-ops).

mike-ops: ack, i'll reserve a node and add a smoke test to check decode divergence > threshold abort.

ci-bot: smoke tests queued for staging-canary: build-5567 -> started.

sara-ml: thanks all. if anyone wants the notebook, ping me and i'll share a link with the visual diffs and token-level traces. :memo:

eva-research: pinged, want to see token diffs. :eyes:

mike-ops: great thread — mark as `kv-quant-mixed` in the bakeoff tracker. :thumbsup:
